ns2:course.label: Comp-Aided Product Realization
ns2:course.description: Computer-aided design, analysis, and prototyping tools used in the produce development process. Principles of computer graphics and geometric modeling, including transformations, coordinate systems, parametric solid modeling, spline curves, and surface modeling. Finite element and kinematics analyses. Rapid prototyping, product dissection, CAD-CAM-CAE operability issues, and CAD collaboration tools. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours. Prerequisite: GE 101 and GE 311.
ns2:course.courseSectionInformation: 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours. Prerequisite: GE 101 and GE 311.
ns2:course.sectionRegistrationNotes: Not intended for students with Freshman or Sophomore class standing. Restricted to BS:General Engineering -UIUC, BS:Mechanical Engineerng -UIUC, BS:Mat Sci Engr:Polymer-UIUC, BFA:Industrial Design -UIUC, or MFA:A&D - Industrial Dsg -UIUC.
